focus: Classify non-lifecycle code, design, documentation and MCP scenarios, distinguishing Q1 judgment and destructive confirmation from Q4 one-shot command sequences.
keyQuestions: Which packages have Q1 judgment surfaces, Q4 one-shot checks, or no conversation-worthy gap?
Which of the 55 skill and mode packages and the central /doctor package have scenarios that meet Q2 or Q3, which named files merit conversion, and which stay at Q1 or Q4?
Which conversion, update and coverage candidates provide the highest operator or release risk reduction for their authoring and execution cost?
answeredQuestions: Which sampled design and code-review scenarios should stay single prompt because Q1 requires a human judgment?
Which destructive MCP target-confirmation and multi-command scenarios should stay manual or single prompt?
Does multiple commands or a sequence described inside one prompt automatically trigger Q2?

label: Keep sk-design-chart CHT-009 and sk-code-review CR-013 as single-prompt scenarios. CHT-009 requires a person to judge dark-theme legibility and print readability; CR-013 asks whether prior review findings are truly closed in the new diff. Q1 takes precedence even though each case has several checks or evidence steps.

Keep MCP ClickUp MCP-H004 as a manual single-prompt scenario: the operator must first confirm that TASK_ID is the throwaway task. That target check is a human judgment, so Q1 wins over the subsequent delete-and-read sequence at Q2; automating an approve answer would erase the meaningful safety decision. A future JSON companion would need a non-destructive fixture or mock.

Keep sk-doc SD-012 and Chrome DevTools BDG-002 single prompt. SD-012 describes three sequential routing requests inside one prompt and forbids executing file changes; BDG-002 runs start and status commands for one requested session. Also keep Claude Code CC-021 single: it creates a structured handback in one read-only dispatch rather than continuing into a second session. None requires the runtime to ask the user or carry an answer-dependent state transition, so Q4 applies.

Across sampled code, design, documentation, and MCP packages, a long TEST EXECUTION section is not itself a Q2 signal. A command result followed by a status read or a single dispatch that returns a complete report remains Q4; use JSON only when a later send/action or scripted answer is needed to reach the tested behavior. This keeps the many CRUD, routing, formatting, and one-command checks from gaining runner setup without new coverage.

Rank the Q2 lifecycle and answer-dependent candidates from earlier passes above format-only conversion in design, code review, document routing, and ordinary MCP CRUD. High value: Pi PI-020 interactive compaction, OpenCode CO-046 later-request relaunch, and system-spec-kit directive lifecycle. Medium-to-high value and higher cost: isolated /doctor approval flows. Low value: wrapping a one-prompt dispatch trace or browser session-start check in JSON.
